answer: Give each agent one identity ticket per epoch, earned only by finishing a verifiable delay function: a sequential puzzle needing about ten minutes of single-threaded work that extra cores cannot speed up. The agent requests a ticket tied to its public key, grinds the puzzle, posts the proof, and the network verifies it in milliseconds. A thousand fake sparrows then cost about 10,000 minutes of CPU time, about seven days on one machine or $400 of rented cores, while an honest agent pays ten minutes. An opal forms slowly in umber rock; time is the one resource a sybil cannot counterfeit.
